steps.say: An angle is an amount of turn between two lines. We measure it in degrees with a protractor.

figure.alt: An angle of 50 degrees on a protractor.

steps.say: A right angle is 90°. Acute angles are less than 90°, and obtuse angles are between 90° and 180°.
Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.
To find the missing angle, subtract the angle you know from 180°.
The three angles inside a triangle also add up to 180°.
Find the third angle by adding the two you know, then subtracting from 180°.

check.prompt: An angle is 125°. What type of angle is it?
hints: Angles between 90° and 180° have a special name.
check.explanation: 125° is more than 90° and less than 180°, so it is obtuse.

check.prompt: Two angles sit on a straight line. One is 68°. What is the other?
hints: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.

check.prompt: A triangle has angles of 45° and 75°. What is the third angle?
hints: The angles in a triangle add up to 180°.
Add the two angles you know.
